newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt to extend bounties - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt to extend bounties - paper.

text.p: The Australian government has decided to extend the expiry date on two contentious budget cuts to business assistance -- the shipbuilding and book printing bounties, The Australian newspaper reported on Tuesday.
The newspaper said the shipbuilding bounty would be extended to December 31 next year, while the book bounty would now end on June 30 next year.
The government would also review the need for any further extension of the shipbuilding bounty during the second half of calendar 1997.
The government had planned to bring forward the abolition of both bounties, as well as those on computers and machine tools.
"The policy reversals follow lobbying from the Minister for Industry Mr (John) Moore, and will cost the government an extra A$18.7 million by the end of next year," the newspaper said.
The changes to the bounties legislation, in total, are worth A$36.0 million to the government's budget in the 1997/98 financial year.

A joint statement from Moore and Treasurer Peter Costello said the government had also considered the views of key Independent senators Brian Harradine and Mal Colston when making its decision to extend the bounties.
Harradine and Colston are key to the passage of many budget bills in the upper house of parliament, the Senate, where the government does not have a majority.
In many cases, they are the only possible sources of the two additional votes the government needs to pass legislation.
